ground_truth: Cyst formation in a persistent thyroglossal duct

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst
Most common congenital midline neck mass in children, typically presents as a painless anterior neck lump that moves with swallowing.
Thyroid nodule
Solitary or dominant thyroid nodule can present as anterior neck mass in adolescents, more common in females.
Dermoid cyst
Congenital midline lesion that can occur in the anterior neck, typically painless and slow-growing.
Goiter (diffuse thyroid enlargement)
Thyroid enlargement from various causes (iodine deficiency, autoimmune thyroiditis) presents as anterior neck swelling in adolescents.
Lymphadenopathy
Enlarged anterior cervical or supraclavicular lymph nodes from infectious or other causes can present as anterior neck mass.
eliminated: None
Insufficient information at this stage to definitively rule out any diagnoses.

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst
Midline neck mass that moves with swallowing, located between hyoid and mandible, is the classic presentation of this congenital remnant.
Dermoid cyst
Midline location superior to hyoid with fluctuance is consistent with this congenital inclusion cyst, though less likely to move with swallowing.
Ectopic thyroid tissue
Midline neck mass that moves with swallowing could represent thyroid tissue along the path of embryologic descent.
Submental lymphadenopathy
Midline location inferior to mandible could represent enlarged lymph nodes, though lack of pain and fever makes reactive causes less likely.
Epidermoid cyst
Fluctuant superficial midline mass is possible, though movement with swallowing would be atypical.
eliminated: Acute thyroiditis
Patient is afebrile with no pain or erythema.
Abscess
Absence of erythema, pain, and fever makes infection unlikely.

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst

Submental lymphadenopathy

Epidermoid cyst

differential: Thyroglossal duct cyst
Confirmed by ultrasound showing midline cystic structure with tract to tongue base and pathologic diagnosis after surgical excision.
Dermoid cyst
Midline neck mass in young patient that can be cystic and fluctuant, though typically does not have a tract to the tongue base.
Epidermoid cyst
Can present as a midline neck mass with fluctuant quality, though less likely given the demonstrated connection to the tongue base.
Ectopic thyroid tissue
Can occur along the thyroglossal duct pathway and present as midline neck mass, though imaging and pathology confirmed cystic rather than solid thyroid tissue.
Thyroid nodule/goiter
Midline neck mass that moves with swallowing, though typically located lower near the thyroid gland and ruled out by normal thyroid function and pathology.
eliminated: Lymphadenopathy
Normal CBC and imaging showed cystic structure rather than lymph node pathology.
Thyroid malignancy
Pathology confirmed benign thyroglossal duct cyst, not malignant tissue.
Abscess/infection
Patient afebrile, no erythema, no pain, and pathology confirmed cystic developmental anomaly rather than infectious process.
Branchial cleft cyst
Typically located laterally rather than midline, and imaging/pathology confirmed thyroglossal origin.

differential: Infected thyroglossal duct cyst
Midline neck mass that moves with swallowing, superior to hyoid, with tenderness and erythema suggests infected congenital cyst along thyroglossal duct pathway.
Thyroglossal duct cyst (non-infected)
Midline location, movement with swallowing, and fluctuance are classic features, though tenderness and erythema are atypical for uncomplicated cyst.
Infected dermoid cyst
Midline congenital cyst can present with tenderness, erythema, and fluctuance when infected, though less commonly moves with swallowing.
Submental lymphadenitis
Infected lymph node in submental space can present with midline tenderness and erythema, though typically less fluctuant and doesn't move with swallowing.
Thyroid nodule with thyroiditis
Midline mass moving with swallowing suggests thyroid origin, with tenderness and erythema indicating inflammatory component, though location superior to hyoid is unusual.
eliminated: Simple thyroglossal duct cyst (uncomplicated)
The presence of tenderness and erythema indicates infection/inflammation rather than simple cyst.

differential: Infected thyroglossal duct cyst

Submental lymphadenitis

Infected median raphe cyst

Normal thyroid function tests make primary thyroid pathology less likely, and location is superior to hyoid rather than at thyroid level.
